Getting started · 3 min read

Daily or Anytime? Find a game that suits your break

One shared challenge or a topic of your choice: here’s where to start.

In this article
  1. Start with the kind of session you want
  2. Choose Daily for a clear next step
  3. Choose Anytime when you have a topic in mind
  4. Use the result to make one decision
  5. Keep your next visit simple
Related gameToday’s Daily games →

Start with the kind of session you want

Some days you want one clear challenge. On others, you want to practise a topic until it feels more familiar. BrainiLab has two ways to choose: Daily challenges provide a shared set for the day, while Anytime games let you choose what to play whenever you visit.

You can start without registering. If you later want to keep progress across devices, sign in through My Stats. Guest play can appear in rankings under a generated alias, so playing without an account does not necessarily mean your result is excluded from a public leaderboard.

Choose Daily for a clear next step

Open the Daily page to see the current challenges and which ones you have completed. The Daily Brain Score combines four scored games, each contributing up to 2,500 points, for a maximum of 10,000. The page is the place to check the actual games in today’s set; do not assume every game on the website contributes to that total.

Brain Mix is a useful place to begin if you like varied questions. Finish a game, read the result and return to the Daily page to choose an unfinished challenge. Different games use different performance measures, so a raw quiz point total and the combined Daily Brain Score are not interchangeable.

After completing today’s set, you can return for another Daily on a later day or move into practice. A replay or past challenge should not be assumed to count as a new scored Daily: check the mode label before starting.

Choose Anytime when you have a topic in mind

The games library offers subject quizzes and different mechanics. Try World Flags for visual recognition, World Capitals for place names, or General Knowledge for a mixture. Where a quiz offers difficulty levels, choose the one that gives you a useful amount of challenge rather than treating the hardest label as a requirement.

If you want a change of pace, try a number or word game. Read its guide first: a worked example can make a new mechanic easier to understand than learning every rule during a timed round. Anytime means you can choose your session; it does not mean every game uses the same rules or the same scoring system.

Use the result to make one decision

Before moving on, ask what the result tells you. Was there a fact you did not know, an instruction you misunderstood, or a question you rushed? Pick one thing to revisit. That gives the next session a purpose without turning every game into homework.

  • A topic caught your attention: follow its subject hub and choose a related quiz.
  • You confused two answers: write down the difference you want to check.
  • You enjoyed the format: try another game with a similar pace.

For example, an uncertain flag answer can lead to our flag practice guide and then another World Flags round. You can also share a completed result using the game’s sharing controls if you want to compare with friends.

Keep your next visit simple

Choose one next action: finish another Daily game, practise a topic, or save your progress with an account. You do not need to do all three in one visit. The next time you open BrainiLab, the Daily page gives you a starting point and the games library gives you alternatives.

BrainiLab+ is optional support for the project. It does not give extra points, attempts or ranking advantages. Read the membership page for current benefits and the advertising status before subscribing; playing and learning do not require Plus.
